key_insight: ATAS reframes long-form video generation around a persistent world state, so the model can consistently revisit places, camera setups, and past events across nonconsecutive shots. This makes screenplay-driven video generation more coherent than simply passing prompts or recent frames forward.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a shared spatial frame and time-indexed memory in agentic video generation, which causes inconsistencies when a scene is revisited later in the story.
method: Compiles a screenplay into shot requests with explicit references to location, camera, and event time.
Retrieves relevant world-state information before generation to provide continuity across shots.
Uses a world-state-centric framework so scenes can be revisited and replayed with spatial and temporal consistency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical blueprint for generating longer, more coherent videos from scripted inputs. It is especially useful for applications that need continuity across scenes, such as storytelling, previsualization, and agentic video pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing screenplay -> shot requests -> world-state retrieval -> video generation
Timeline graphic illustrating nonconsecutive scene revisits with consistent time references
Scene map or 3D layout icon showing persistent spatial world state
Before/after comparison of naive frame-passing vs ATAS consistency
paper_title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
paper_authors: Weijie Wang, Haomin Zhang, Ye Li, Akide Liu, Zeyu Zhang
